A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2P research. All 14 pages of each version, including the supplementary text, equations, figures, tables and prompt templates, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition, captioning and personalized VQA results, along with component, verification and retrieval ablations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds recognition results for Yo’LLaVA trained with a MiniCPM-o 2.6 backbone.

M1.justification: R2P retains the same database construction, multimodal retrieval, attribute-focused reasoning, cross-modal verification and conditional pairwise reasoning. Its backbone and supplementary prompt templates are unchanged; the newly adapted Yo’LLaVA model is a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate recognition and captioning on MyVLM, Yo’LLaVA and PerVA, and personalized VQA on Yo’LLaVA. The added PerVA overview documents existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Yo’LLaVA w/ MiniCPM-o 2.6 to the Yo’LLaVA recognition comparison. The existing comparators remain, including RAP, GPT-4V + Vprompt and MiniCPM-o + prompt; other comparison sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a control that trains Yo’LLaVA with MiniCPM-o 2.6 replacing its original VLM, and revises PerVA’s reported retail concept count from 70 to 69. Existing metrics, cropping, K=3 and single-reference settings remain unchanged. Newly disclosed split sizes do not establish that PerVA was resplit.

E4.justification: The added backbone-controlled comparison tests whether R2P’s advantage can be attributed to its underlying VLM. Existing component, verification and retrieval ablations and the qualitative hallucination example remain unchanged, including v1 Tables 6–11 matched to v2 Tables 7–12.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 in both versions reports averaging over three different seeds. Neither version adds confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or another uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises baseline captioning results: on MyVLM, MyVLM changes from 84.7 to 0.02 and Yo’LLaVA from 86.7 to 0.1; on Yo’LLaVA, Yo’LLaVA changes from 81.6 to 0.2. This changes baseline rankings and apparent effectiveness. The added backbone comparator scores 62.5 weighted recognition accuracy. R2P’s own numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal problem formulation, assumptions and Equations (1)–(8) are retained. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs that distinguish it from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free personalization through fingerprint-based retrieval and reasoning, the PerVA benchmark, and state-of-the-art personalization performance. The rewritten conclusion does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the advantage over the new backbone-matched comparator to R2P’s reasoning procedure and explains poor training-based captioning through dependence on explicitly supplied concept names. It also interprets PerVA’s category imbalance as realistic. Existing limitations concerning computational cost and cluttered scenes remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with reported code and data availability through a project-page link. New Section 8.1 and Table 6 provide previously missing PerVA split and category statistics, including 59,392 training images, 8,090 test images and 329 database references. These substantially expand access and dataset reproducibility information; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 52 works and retain the related-work discussion and training-free novelty positioning. Reference-page backlinks change, but the cited research and its substantive relationship to R2P do not.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites implementation details, baseline and results discussion, and the conclusion. It adds acknowledgments and a PerVA overview subsection and renumbers the supplement. The introduction, related work and method narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the PerVA distribution table and a comparator row in Table 1. Existing supplementary tables are renumbered and relocated, and Figure 5 is resized to accommodate text below it. Figure content and the overall two-column presentation are retained.

improvement.justification: The PerVA documentation, code/data access information and backbone-controlled comparison modestly improve reproducibility and assessment of the method. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies introduced around the revised results: Section 5.2 retains a 5.5-point captioning margin although updated Table 1 implies 7.4 points, and claims a 4.8-point negative-accuracy advantage where the table implies 4.2. The core method and R2P results are unchanged.
